**Status fixes against the pre-registered bars:**
- Supported: H7.1.1 (E030) and H7.2.3 (E038, confirmed by the rerun E039).
- Refuted: H7.1.2 (E034), H7.2.1 (E035: time saving too small) and H6.3.1/H6.3 (E037).
- Retired: H7.2.2. The E033 spectrum analysis shows that 3-step Polar-Express coefficients are already worse than the fixed ones, so 2 steps would be worse still.
- H5 keeps its refuted status. Its E020+/E024+ evidence tokens follow the opposite sign convention, which is noted in the reason; I could not edit the tokens themselves.

**Restated hypotheses:**
- **H7** keeps its main claim: Muon was the optimizer lever (supported, confidence lowered to 0.55). Its "the hyperparameters still have room" clause is closed. Momentum, LR, Newton-Schulz step count and label smoothing each came back flat, and E035's gain turned out to be noise. **H7.2** now says only cutting the step count reduces Muon's per-step cost. The momentum buffer is too small for an fp16 buffer to save measurable time.
- **H2.4** now admits that the power-cap model fails in the 16/24 px phases (E038 saved ~2 ms per removed step). It also records that gains coming from per-step overhead are at higher risk of not carrying over to the 300 W PCIe judging card than gains from cutting FLOPs.
- **H2.8** drops the "diminishing returns" claim. Once E026's lucky run is averaged out, the cost per 16 px epoch looks roughly linear. E041 is re-read as inconclusive rather than refuted.
- **H2.10** and H2.10.1 are lowered. The measured costs make "move epochs to 16 px and spend the savings on more 32 px training" roughly break-even or worse.
- **H4** now uses E038/E039 as a second rerun pair, notes that its noise estimate rests on only n=2 pairs, and flags that the seeds 3-10 margin check has not been redone on the bs 1536 tip.
- **H4.2** is supported: E040 replicated E029 almost exactly, and E035's apparent gain disappeared.

**New hypotheses:**
- **N1:** per-phase batch size (fast.ai, OLMo), with N1a (bs 2048 at low resolution, 1024 at 32 px) and N1b (bs 3072 at low resolution after a short small-batch start).
- **N2:** CUDA-graphing the step for the low-res shapes only (N2a), gated on N2b, a per-phase CUDA-event timing under H2.4.
- **N3/N3a:** warmup retune at ~256 steps.
- **N4/N4a:** LR floor under Muon.
- **N5/N5a:** a group-2 width retest under Muon (a FLOP-reducing lever).
- **N6:** seeds 3-10 margin check on the E038 tip.
- **N7:** the unbundled determinism probe.
- **N8:** an offline check of AOL preconditioning before any scored run.

**Suggested order before any further cuts:**
1. Run N6, N7 and H2.4.1/N2b, which are cheap and untimed.
2. Confirm whether E038's parent commit includes E035's renorm change.
3. Run N1a, the most promising lever.

Open Lvl1 hypotheses: H2, H4, H6."}

updates.statement: At full resolution the A100-SXM4 trains at its 400 W cap, so time for the net's fwd/bwd tracks GPU energy, and CPU gaps hidden behind GPU work cost nothing (E004, E010, E011; all SGD, 32 px). This does NOT hold in the small-map 16/24 px phases. There, bs 1024->1536 saved ~2 ms per removed step (E038), twice the ~1 ms Muon cost. Per-step work beyond Muon (SGD foreach step, lookahead, launch gaps, small-kernel inefficiency) therefore costs wall time there. Transfer risk: on the official 300 W PCIe card, GPU work is slower, so per-step and launch overhead is a smaller share. Levers whose gain is per-step (batch size, CUDA graphs) are less likely to transfer than FLOP-reducing levers. Prefer FLOP-reducing levers on local ties.
updates.reason: E038 contradicts the pure energy-bound model for the low-res phases (review). The PCIe transfer caveat was added per the review. Confidence lowered because the model is now known to be phase-dependent.
E038's ~2 ms per removed step makes the predicted pattern (32 px power-bound, 16/24 px below the cap) more likely. Still unmeasured, untimed and cheap.

updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work and per-step overhead drive the score. The strongest schedule lever is cheap early epochs: 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px (E026), and 24 px is the minimum useful bridge (E032, E041). Measured epoch cost relative to 32 px: 16 px 0.32x, 20 px ~0.51x, 24 px 0.57x, 26 px 0.75x, 28 px 0.79x, 30 px 0.95x (E013, E026, E041). Narrowing (E017) and widening (E005) were refuted only under SGD. In the low-res phases a per-step cost (~2 ms/step at bs 1024, E038) is a large share, which is why bs 1536 paid off. Every Muon schedule so far kept 8 total epochs and a single global batch size.
updates.reason: Integrated E038/E041 and the review's per-step finding. This opens per-phase batch size, a low-res CUDA graph, and a Muon-era width retest as children.

updates.statement: Accuracy and timing noise set the usable margin. The compiled SGD recipe is bit-deterministic per seed (E002). The compiled-Muon progressive recipes are not: identical reruns moved single seeds by up to ~0.6 pp (E028, E039). The run-to-run sd of a 3-seed mean is roughly 0.1-0.15 pp, but it rests on only n=2 identical-rerun pairs (E026/E028: 0.22 pp apart; E038/E039: 0.00 apart), so it is poorly estimated. Gaps under ~0.3-0.4 pp between single runs should not be read as signal. Current tip E038 (bs 1536): 0.7542 on both runs, only 0.11 pp above the local 0.753 bar. The seeds 3-10 check (mean 0.7553, sd 0.22 pp) was done on the E026 recipe, not on E038. Rule for a new tip: a 3-seed mean >=0.755, or two runs averaging >=0.7535. Log every identical rerun as a variance sample. Time noise ~0.1-0.5%.
updates.reason: Added E039 as the second rerun pair and stated the sample count, per the review. Flagged that the official-margin extrapolation has not been redone for the bs 1536 tip.

E040 replicated E029 almost exactly (0.7522 vs 0.7523), and E035's apparent +0.18 pp vanished in its successors (E040, E041 vs the family estimate). This confirms that single near-threshold reads select for luck. E039 confirmed E038 under the two-run rule.
E036 achieved determinism but bundled two changes at +9.8% time. Unresolved which change restored determinism. The unbundled probe is added as a new child.

new.statement: Per-phase batch size: per-step costs dominate the cheap 16/24 px phases (E038), while the 32 px tail is closer to energy-bound and binding for accuracy (E010, E025). A large batch in the low-res phases and a smaller batch at 32 px should capture bs 1536's time saving without paying its ~0.13-0.30 pp accuracy cost in the tail. Large batches may hurt most at the very start, where the critical batch size is near zero (OLMo).

On the tip lineage, use bs 2048 for the 2@16 + 2@24 epochs and bs 1024 for the 4@32 epochs. LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm are indexed by samples seen, and the SGD groups are scaled per phase by the kilostep rule (Muon lr/momentum unchanged). All batch/resolution shapes are compiled and warmed up in build. Prediction: time <=5.26 s (within +1% of E038) and 3-seed accuracy >=0.755. If time is >=5.35 s, the per-step-bound explanation of E038 is wrong.

On the E038 tip (bs 1536), raise only the 16/24 px phases to bs 3072, but keep the first 0.5 epoch at bs 1536 as a small-batch start. The 32 px tail stays at bs 1536, with schedules indexed by samples. Prediction: time <=5.05 s (>=3% below E038) with 3-seed accuracy >=0.7535.

Low-res phases are launch- or per-step-bound (E038), unlike full-res SGD where graphing and fusion gave nothing (E011). Capturing the whole train step (fwd, bwd, SGD foreach, compiled Muon, lookahead) in a CUDA graph for the 16/24 px shapes only removes idle gaps there. Caveats: the Fable CIFAR-10 record found graphs near-neutral, and per-step gains transfer poorly to the 300 W PCIe judge.

On the E038 tip, CUDA-graph the full step for the 16 px and 24 px shapes only, captured and warmed up in build on synthetic data, with static input buffers and the LR passed as 0-d tensors. Prediction: time drops by >=2% (<=5.11 s) with 3-seed accuracy >=0.7535. Gate: run only if the N2b/H2.4.1 measurement shows wall time >=1.3x GPU-busy time in those phases.
Untimed CUDA-event and profiler timing of the E038 tip per phase. Per step, wall time exceeds GPU-busy time by >=30% at 16 px and >=15% at 24 px, and by <10% at 32 px. Observational only.

bs 1536 cut the run to ~256 steps, but the LR warmup was only rescaled from a schedule tuned at ~408 SGD steps. Warmup length is untested and zero-cost, and a retuned warmup recovered a near-miss in an airbench96 agent loop.

On the E038 tip, halving the LR warmup length (in steps; everything else unchanged) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7562 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7542 two-run mean) at equal time. If both halving and doubling stay within +/-0.15 pp, warmup is closed.

The LR floor (0.07x) and the lookahead-EMA ramp were tuned under SGD (E015). Muon's normalized updates fit faster, so a lower Muon-group LR floor (~0.05, as in public Muon recipes) or a shorter final EMA may suit it better.
On the E038 tip, set the Muon-group LR floor from 0.07x to 0.05x and leave everything else unchanged. Prediction: 3-seed accuracy >=0.7562 at equal time. A result within +/-0.15 pp closes it.

Muon flattened the accuracy-vs-epochs slope (0.54 vs 0.95 pp/epoch, E020), so the width cut refuted under SGD (E017: 0.115 pp per 1%) may now trade at or below the current exchange rate. It is a FLOP-reducing lever, so it should transfer to the 300 W PCIe judge better than per-step levers.

On the E038 tip, narrow group 2 from 384 to 352 channels (recompiled and warmed up in build). Prediction: time drops >=3.5% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.2 pp vs 0.7542, i.e. <=0.06 pp per 1%, beating bs 1536's 0.064.

Untimed side check: the E038 tip code run through the benchmark's trial code on seeds 3-10 has a mean >=0.7530 and lies within 0.15 pp of its seeds 0-2 two-run mean (0.7542). Then the official 40-seed mean clears 0.75 with >=0.25 pp to spare.

Unbundled determinism probe on the E038 tip: compile the Muon update with mode='default', keep cudnn.benchmark=True, and change nothing else. An untimed seed-0 repeat in a fresh process is bit-identical to the scored seed 0, and time is within +1% of 5.216 s. If it is not bit-identical, the nondeterminism comes from cuDNN benchmark picks, not Muon autotune.

Offline on the E033-captured Muon inputs: AOL preconditioning (X0 scaled by diag(rowsum|X0^T X0|)^-1/2) followed by 2 fixed-quintic iterations puts >=50% of singular values in [0.7, 1.3] (matching 3 plain iterations at 0.56). Only if this holds is a scored run worth it, with an expected saving of ~0.32 ms/step (~1.5%).

structured_output.summary:
I brought the tree in line with the evidence, the review and the search.

**Status fixes against the pre-registered bars:**
- Supported: H7.1.1 (E030) and H7.2.3 (E038, confirmed by the rerun E039).
- Refuted: H7.1.2 (E034), H7.2.1 (E035: time saving too small) and H6.3.1/H6.3 (E037).
- Retired: H7.2.2. The E033 spectrum analysis shows that 3-step Polar-Express coefficients are already worse than the fixed ones, so 2 steps would be worse still.
- H5 keeps its refuted status. Its E020+/E024+ evidence tokens follow the opposite sign convention, which is noted in the reason; I could not edit the tokens themselves.

**Restated hypotheses:**
- **H7** keeps its main claim: Muon was the optimizer lever (supported, confidence lowered to 0.55). Its "the hyperparameters still have room" clause is closed. Momentum, LR, Newton-Schulz step count and label smoothing each came back flat, and E035's gain turned out to be noise. **H7.2** now says only cutting the step count reduces Muon's per-step cost. The momentum buffer is too small for an fp16 buffer to save measurable time.
- **H2.4** now admits that the power-cap model fails in the 16/24 px phases (E038 saved ~2 ms per removed step). It also records that gains coming from per-step overhead are at higher risk of not carrying over to the 300 W PCIe judging card than gains from cutting FLOPs.
- **H2.8** drops the "diminishing returns" claim. Once E026's lucky run is averaged out, the cost per 16 px epoch looks roughly linear. E041 is re-read as inconclusive rather than refuted.
- **H2.10** and H2.10.1 are lowered. The measured costs make "move epochs to 16 px and spend the savings on more 32 px training" roughly break-even or worse.
- **H4** now uses E038/E039 as a second rerun pair, notes that its noise estimate rests on only n=2 pairs, and flags that the seeds 3-10 margin check has not been redone on the bs 1536 tip.
- **H4.2** is supported: E040 replicated E029 almost exactly, and E035's apparent gain disappeared.

**New hypotheses:**
- **N1:** per-phase batch size (fast.ai, OLMo), with N1a (bs 2048 at low resolution, 1024 at 32 px) and N1b (bs 3072 at low resolution after a short small-batch start).
- **N2:** CUDA-graphing the step for the low-res shapes only (N2a), gated on N2b, a per-phase CUDA-event timing under H2.4.
- **N3/N3a:** warmup retune at ~256 steps.
- **N4/N4a:** LR floor under Muon.
- **N5/N5a:** a group-2 width retest under Muon (a FLOP-reducing lever).
- **N6:** seeds 3-10 margin check on the E038 tip.
- **N7:** the unbundled determinism probe.
- **N8:** an offline check of AOL preconditioning before any scored run.

**Suggested order before any further cuts:**
1. Run N6, N7 and H2.4.1/N2b, which are cheap and untimed.
2. Confirm whether E038's parent commit includes E035's renorm change.
3. Run N1a, the most promising lever.

Open Lvl1 hypotheses: H2, H4, H6.
